verdict.reasoning: Patient states diarrhea for past three days and going to toilet 5–6 times a day: “I’ve been having, uh, diarrhoea, for like, let's say past three days…”, “around, five to six times a day”, and confirms “definitely watery… loose stools”.

Transcript: “it started with vomiting, so I vomited a couple of times. Uh, but then, that went away”. Number of episodes (“a couple of times”) and resolution are supported, but “twice” is a specific count not stated; ‘couple’ could be approximate, so exact ‘twice’ is added detail.
Patient: “Yes, it's definitely, definitely watery, uh, loose stools, yeah.”
Doctor: “Any blood in your stools?” Patient: “Yes, I could see some.”
Doctor: “with the diarrhea have you noticed any other symptoms, like tummy pain?” Patient: “Uh, not, not really, no.”
Patient: “I feel like I don't drink enough… I… feel dehydrated again.” and earlier “I feel very dehydrated.”
Doctor: “have you managed to eat anything, solids?” Patient: “Uh, not much, not much. So just a little bit, but I don't feel… I have appetite.”
Patient: “I feel very weak though.”
Patient: “probably at, at the beginning I was feeling I had a bit of temperature.”
Patient: “but now I feel, I feel kind of fine.” in context of discussing fever/temperature implies now afebrile.
Doctor: “Any headaches or muscle pains?” Patient: “Not, not really, no.” This includes denial of headaches.
Same exchange: “Any headaches or muscle pains?” Patient: “Not, not really, no.” Denies myalgias.
Doctor asks about takeaway/dodgy food: “Did you have any takeaway food, or any dodgy restaurant food?” Patient: “Uh, not that I remember, no.” indicating no known food trigger.
Doctor: “Have you been around anyone unwell, with diarrhea recently…?” Patient: “Hmm, not that I know, not that I.” indicating no known sick contacts.
Patient: “I do suffer of asthma.”
Patient: “I do have my inhalers… I use infrequently”, Doctor clarifies: “Is that the blue inhaler? Blue inhaler.” indicating a short-acting beta-agonist used as needed.
Doctor: “Do you have any allergies to medications?” Patient: “Um, not that I know of.”
Patient: “my father has, high uh, well used to have high blood pressure.”
Patient: “He actually, so he actually died, of, bowel cancer, like ten years ago.”
Patient: “my mother… she has diabetes.” Doctor: “Do you know if that's type one or type two?” Patient: “Uh, it's type two.”
Doctor: “Who lives at home with you?” Patient: “Ohh I, I live alone.”
Doctor: “What do you do for work?” Patient: “I'm a software engineer.”
Patient: “these last three days I've been feeling, really unwell, so I couldn't work.”
Doctor: “regarding your smoking and alcohol. Do you do either of those?” Patient: “…I drink infrequently, like socially let's say, and I don't smoke.”
Same quote: “I drink infrequently, like socially let's say, and I don't smoke.”
Doctor: “I think you're probably suffering from what we call gastroenteritis, uh which essentially is just a, a tummy bug.”

Patient repeatedly reports feeling very dehydrated, poor intake, and frequent watery diarrhea; doctor emphasizes fluid replacement, implying risk of dehydration: “you can drink plenty of fluids… help replenish any… you may have lost.” This is a direct clinical inference.
Patient: “I do have my inhalers… I use infrequently” indicates intermittent asthma.
Asthma inhaler described as blue (short-acting reliever) and used infrequently/as needed: “I do have my inhalers… I use infrequently… Is that the blue inhaler? Blue inhaler.”
Doctor: “the things you can do to really help yourself get better soon… you can drink plenty of fluids.”
Doctor: “you can get things from the pharmacy, which is called Dioralyte… it's a type of fluid replacement drink.”
Doctor: “you can take some Paracetamol if you're feeling feverish and weak.”
Doctor: “I would probably advise you to continue taking time off work for next day or two, until you get better.”
Doctor: “normally you have to be diarrhea-free for about twenty four to forty eight hours, before you return back to work.”
Doctor: “Let's see how the next few days go. And if you're still not better next week, I want you to come back and see me.”
